utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, is this the woman to whom you returned that money during your leave between the 16th and 19th after the killing of her husband?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the woman in question. She was involved in some black market activities, and this is the certificate in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown document D46/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, would you please identify this document, but try to be as brief as possible. We only have ten minutes left for today.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the list of soldiers who were killed, which list was made by the Public Security Station of Prijedor on the 22nd of June, 1992. This list is made according to their dates of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Would you please turn to the next page and have a look at the 12th of June, 1992, and tell us who was killed on the 12th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Strahilo Stanojevic, father's name Vid. I'm using the usual police wording: Stanislav Stanojevic, father's name Vid, from Lamovita. This is the husband of the lady to whom I returned the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you return the money after the burial of this gentleman, Mr. Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was supposed to come. That is what Zeljko told me, and he told me that she had already seen someone else for that purpose, but because her case was not processed yet and the status of that money was that of a temporary confiscation, and he only told me that a decision had been made that the money should be returned to her. And this is what I did during the period of time which I spent on sick leave, that is, from the 16th until the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is that the same period of time which was mentioned by your wife?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and she knows about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I will ask several very brief questions at this point; however, before I do that, today you testified that Mr. Drljaca was the only man who could release prisoners from Omarska. In my opening statement, I mentioned a letter which was written by Franjo Komarica, the archbishop Franjo Komarica.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I should like Exhibit D47/1 to be shown and distributed, and the document, of course, to be shown to Mr. Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, I should like to draw your attention to paragraph 3 of Bishop Komarica's letter. First of all, let me ask you who this letter was addressed to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was addressed to Mr. Simo Drljaca, Public Security Station Chief. The letter was sent by the bishop of Banja Luka, that is, the bishop's office of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Would you please have a look at the last page and tell us who signed the letter.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bishop of Banja Luka, Dr. Franjo Komarica.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who else was this letter sent to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the president of the municipal assembly of Prijedor, Milo Stakic, to General Talic, and also to the apostolic nuncio in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Would you now please have a look at the pertinent passage, that is, the third paragraph of the letter?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: "Since you could not at that time grant my request to visit my priest, the Honourable Mr. Stipo Sosic, the parish priest from Ljubija who has been in the Omarska camp since the 15th of June 1992, you promised to call me within two days and let me know what was happening to him and why he was in the camp at all." Mr. Meakic in his capacity as the Omarska Police Station Department commander within whose authority was the security service, was he able to grant visits to the camp to any individual?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he have any authority to enable contact of the detained persons there with their members -- with the members of their family?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who was able to do that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca was the only person who had authority to do that. That can be seen from other documents as well, and this document testifies to that fact as well. And we have seen orders where it is explicitly stated that it was Simo Drljaca who could allow entry/departure from the centre, and also all other contact with the detained persons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't want to go back to the document; we have seen it a number of times. It's an order on the 31st of May, 1992, an order issued by Simo Drljaca. You have seen it many times. Did that order contain all elements of command structure and organisation of the place?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The order shows what I have just mentioned. It's a classical type of order which provides for all tasks and elements of work for various departments, and where he explicitly states that superior officers are in charge of submitting a daily report to him. I think that even the time limit is mentioned in the decision; that is, that they were to report to him on the situation on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I now have a series of very brief questions. I don't wish to discuss the interview with Bob Reid in detail. I just want to know whether he asked you whether you could issue any authorisation to anyone in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Sorry, whether you could issue orders to anyone in Omarska. Could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon Bob Reid's question whether I could issue orders, I answered no, and I can repeat that here once again: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Reid ask you whether Mr. Kos, Mr. Radic, and Mr. Gruban had the authority to issue any kind of order to anyone?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he asked me that, and I told him that they did not have that authority. They could not issue any order of that kind, any order at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you today, once again, whether the three individuals actually issued orders. I'm not talking about their ability to issue orders.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they never issued any orders, nor did they have ability to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, did Mr. Reid ask you about an individual by the name of Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would it be possible to ask counsel to indicate the page, for the record, so we can have a look at it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Kvocka is testifying about what he spoke. If we now read this interview, we will have the same scenario as with Ms. Somers. I think that it is very easy for Ms. Somers to check on this by comparing the transcript of Mr. Kvocka's testimony of today and the interview with Mr. Bob Reid, and she can even point to certain inconsistencies if there are any such inconsistencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, are you sure you want to offer that -- could you please tell that to Ms. Somers tomorrow? Very well. Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Of course it would not be necessary to have anything read out now. It's just to assist us whether that was said in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think that this is a very good solution. I think time has come for us to wind up for today. I hope that Mr. Simic can do his colleague a favour and give her the page number. I think that we will stop here and come back tomorrow at twenty minutes past nine. I think that Mr. Kvocka also needs some rest. Until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of February, 2001, at 9.20 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.05 p.m.,
